# Exact centroid-shell compensation failure and a strict-noheavy example

The archived dominated-mean theorem already bounds centroid displacement
by BM surplus. The new content here is an exact signed, all-dimensional
cap-surplus identity and a rational planar example in which the actual
raw depth of the moving middle centroid decreases despite strict
noheavy and actual nested enlargement. This is not an OC counterexample
or a claim that the globally optimal center becomes worse.

## 1. Actual three-fiber simplex enlargement

Let d>=1, let T={x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1}, and write V=|T|=1/d! and
g=(1/(d+1),...,1/(d+1)). For r>=1 define

    C_r={ (z,x): -1<=z<=1, x_i>=0,
                      sum_i x_i<=r-(r-1)|z| }.

The final inequality is the intersection of two affine halfspaces.
Thus C_r is a compact full-dimensional convex body. Its exact integer
fibers are T,rT,T at -1,0,1. Also C_1 subset C_r, and the middle
centroid is g_r=rg whereas the endpoint-centroid midpoint is g.
The centroid Jensen defect is exactly (r-1)g. The whole-fiber BM
root surplus is (r-1)V^(1/d), and the added mixed volume is

    Delta=(r^d-1)V.

The source point (0,g_r) remains in the original common simplex T
whenever r<= (d+1)/d, since sum_i(g_r)_i=rd/(d+1)<=1.

## 2. Exact signed directional cap identity

Put c=d/(d+1), Gamma=c^d, and assume 1<=r<=1/c. Consider the zero-tilt
ambient cap through the moving source

    H_r^+={ (z,x):sum_i x_i>=rc }.

The middle contribution is (1-Gamma)r^d V. Each endpoint contributes
[1-Gamma r^d]V, including zero at the boundary r=1/c. Thus

    mu_r(H_r^+)=[2+(1-3Gamma)r^d]V,

and, comparing with the corresponding cap through the original centroid,

    mu_r(H_r^+)-mu_1(H_1^+)=(1-3Gamma)Delta<0       (r>1). (1)

The strict sign uses Gamma>1/3. The ordinary opposite caps have zero
d-volume on their boundaries, so their masses sum to the total. Hence

    mu_r(H_r^-)-mu_1(H_1^-)=3Gamma Delta>0,          (2)

where H_r^-={sum_i x_i<=rc}. These are two opposite signs of the same
continuous normal, not a restriction to base-parallel halfspaces in
the claimed full problem.

There is an exact slice accounting behind (1). If s=sum_i x_i, then
the projected volume density of T is

    rho(s)=s^(d-1)/(d-1)! for 0<s<1,

and that of rT has the same density up to s=r. The added middle shell
has volume Delta and lies wholly above the moving threshold rc<=1.
Moving the cut from c to rc loses

    integral_c^(rc) rho(s) ds=Gamma Delta

from EACH of the three old pieces. Thus its whole positive added
shell contributes Delta but the three lost slabs cost 3Gamma Delta.
No unspecified transport loss or approximation is present.

The moment identity is equally explicit:

    integral_(rT minus T) x dx=(r^(d+1)-1)Vg,
    integral_(rT minus T) (x-rg) dx=(r-1)Vg.

It recovers the exact centroid displacement, while (1) shows that the
associated surplus does not supply nonnegative compensation in every
through-centroid cap direction. The opposite direction gains the full
amount in (2). These identities hold with strict noheavy whenever
r^d<2, since then the largest whole fiber is less than half the total.

## 3. A self-contained planar product-depth certificate

For d=2, the product source {-1,0,1} times T has exact raw depth
4V/3 at (0,g), g=(1/3,1/3). Here is an elementary all-direction proof.

For a nonconstant affine functional on a uniform triangle, normalize
its three vertex values to 0,p,1, 0<=p<=1. Its projected mean is
m=(1+p)/3. The normalized CDF is

    G(x)=x^2/p                    for 0<=x<=p,
         1-(1-x)^2/(1-p)         for p<=x<=1,

with zero and one outside [0,1]. Endpoint cases p=0,1 are the
continuous limits and have no atoms. For p<=1/2, m>=p and m<=1/2.
Set J(h)=G(m-h)+G(m+h), h>=0. On [0,m-p], J is decreasing.
On [m-p,m], it is convex, with its minimum at h=1/3 and value

    J(1/3)=(8+2p)/9>=8/9.

These assertions follow by differentiating the two displayed quadratics;
in the mixed region J''=2/p-2/(1-p)>=0 and
J'=2(1-2p)(h-1/3)/(p(1-p)). After h=m the lower CDF is zero and J
increases to one, then stays one. Consequently

    8/9<=J(h)<=max(2G(m),1)<=10/9,

where G(m)=1-(2-p)^2/[9(1-p)] lies in [1/2,5/9]. For p>=1/2,
reflection x->1-x replaces p by 1-p and J by 2-J, preserving the
same interval. The cases p=0,1,1/2 follow directly or by continuity.
Also every through-centroid one-sided triangle cap has fraction at
least 4/9, from the same formula and reflection.

For a nonvertical ambient halfspace through (0,g), the two endpoint
thresholds are opposite shifts about m. Their captured fractions sum
to 2-J(h)>=8/9, while the middle cap contributes at least 4/9.
Thus its mass is at least (4/3)V. A purely integer-coordinate cap
contains the full middle and one full endpoint, of mass 2V. Moving
any containing halfspace to the source does not increase its mass,
so all closed containing ambient halfspaces are covered.

Equality occurs at zero integer tilt in a canonical vertex cap,
whose three triangle pieces each have fraction 4/9. Thus the raw
depth is exactly 4V/3. The three canonical middle traces cover the
middle plane, and endpoint fibers are isolated by vertical caps of
mass V, so this is also the product source's global maximum.

## 4. Strict-noheavy raw depth loss at the moving centroid

Now let d=2 and choose the exact rational parameter

    r=141/100,  g_r=(47/100,47/100).

Its middle volume r^2 V=(19881/10000)V is strictly below half of
the total (39881/10000)V; the gap is (119/20000)V. Its centroid is
still in the original common simplex, since its coordinate sum is
47/50<1. Consider the actual oblique halfspace

    H={ (z,x,y):x+y+(3/50)z>=47/50 }.

It passes through (0,g_r). On the first endpoint its threshold is
1, giving a supporting face of zero area. On the second endpoint
the threshold is 22/25, giving area [1-(22/25)^2]V=(141/625)V.
The middle captured area is

    [r^2-(47/50)^2]V=(2209/2000)V.

The total is therefore

    mu_r(H)=(13301/10000)V
             =(4/3)V-(97/30000)V < (4/3)V.         (3)

By Section 3, (3) is strictly smaller than the actual raw depth of
the original middle centroid in the original product source. The
moving middle centroid's actual raw depth is at most (3), so its
raw depth genuinely decreases. This is stronger than a merely
negative difference of two noncritical directional cap masses.

At the unchanged old centroid (0,g), every cap in the enlarged source
still has mass at least 4V/3, because the original source is contained
in the enlarged one. Thus the globally optimal depth has not been
claimed to decrease; the enlarged body has an explicitly better
actual middle point than its own ordinary centroid. No assertion
that the displayed oblique cap attains depth at g_r is needed.

The example does not threaten OC. For instance the retained old point
already pays 4V/3, whereas the n=1,d=2 target is
(2/9)(39881/10000)V, which is strictly smaller. The obstruction is to
an unconditional positive directional surplus compensation or a
monotone raw-depth rule along the ordinary fiber-centroid path.
